metadata.title: Identify Files
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Identify which files and directories need to be processed based on flexible criteria (patterns, scope descriptions, or both). Use when you need to create a comprehensive list of files for subsequent processing.

prerequisites: Context parameters from process.json or memory.json
specificActions: Follow the substeps below - workflow depends on search depth mode (simple or deep)
Simple mode: Agent decides search approach based on available parameters
Deep mode: Exhaustive search with tracking to ensure completeness
tools: codebase_search - Understand scope and identify targets
bestPractices: Apply exclusions during discovery when possible (more efficient)
Log progress periodically for large file sets (>1000 files)
Use simple search (default) for most cases - it's fast and efficient
Save results to separate JSON file to keep memory.json clean
For hidden directories (starting with .), glob_file_search may not find files - use list_dir as backup

SHARED INFRASTRUCTURE SCOPE EXPANSION: When the concept being changed affects shared infrastructure (step definitions, type definitions, template schemas, APIs), automatically include ALL repositories that consume or define that infrastructure. For example, if step definitions change how they declare memory usage, all template repos containing step definitions must be in scope — not just the framework repo.

substeps.name: Read Context Parameters
substeps.description: Read search parameters and determine search mode
actions: Read filePatterns, scope, excludePatterns, searchDepth, includeMatchReason from context
Determine search mode: 'simple' (default) or 'deep'
Document parameters in log.json

substeps.name: Handle Deep Search Mode
actions: List all files recursively using list_dir
Create tracking JSON file to track progress
Iterate and check each file against criteria
Verify all files have been checked

substeps.name: Handle Simple Search Mode
substeps.description: Fast search using glob, grep, codebase_search (default mode)
actions: Agent decides search approach based on available parameters
If patterns available: Use glob_file_search
If scope available: Use codebase_search + list_dir + grep
If both: Agent decides how to combine

substeps.name: Broad Text-Reference Search
substeps.description: Search for all textual references to target files, directories, or concepts — not just structured references like JSON arrays
actions: Identify the key names being targeted (file names, directory names, concept names)
Run broad grep searches across ALL file types (.json, .md, .ts, .js, .py, .sh, etc.) for these names
Search for references in: inline text/comments, markdown links, import statements, documentation prose, directory listings, type definitions, and configuration files
Compare broad search results against the structured search results from substep 3 — flag any files found by broad search but missed by structured search
Log the delta: how many additional files were found by broad search

substeps.name: Cross-Repository Scope Verification
substeps.description: Verify whether the search scope covers all repositories that may reference the targets
actions: Review the list of project paths provided in the process parameters
Consider: are there related repositories, downstream consumers, or other codebases that might reference the identified targets?
If the process involves shared infrastructure (templates, types, APIs, UI components), check for references in consuming repositories
If additional repositories are identified, extend the search to cover them and document the scope expansion
Log: repositories checked and whether scope was expanded

substeps.name: Apply Exclusion Patterns
substeps.description: Filter out excluded files from results
actions: Apply common exclusions (node_modules, .git, dist, build, bin, obj, etc.)
Apply custom exclusions from excludePatterns parameter
Log exclusions applied and files removed count

substeps.name: Create File Identification Report
substeps.description: Document the search results and flag content preservation needs
actions: Document search approach used
Include summary: total files found, excluded files count
Note any issues encountered

For files marked for deletion: check if any contain content that belongs elsewhere or should be preserved (e.g., useful documentation misplaced in a directory being removed). Flag these with contentPreservationRequired: true and describe the preservation action needed.

substeps.name: Save Results to JSON File and Update Memory
substeps.description: Save results and update memory reference
actions: Save file list to identified-files.json
Format: array of paths (default) or array of {path, matchReason, contentPreservationRequired?, preservationAction?} objects
For any file flagged for content preservation, include contentPreservationRequired: true and preservationAction describing what to do (e.g., 'Move to docs/claude/ before deleting parent directory')
Record via add-memory-entry --topic identified-files: file count and path to results JSON

substeps.name: End-Step: Compliance Check
substeps.description: Verify principles were followed in this step
actions: Verify: Was log.json updated for any user interactions?
Verify: Were mandatory actions confirmed with output?

Log problems: If any problems, errors, workarounds, or unexpected situations were encountered during this step, log them via add-log-entry --problems '["description of problem 1", ...]'. This feeds the continuous-improvement step's analysis.
Output: '✓ Step completed in compliance with operating principles'

flow.description: Read parameters → Choose search mode (simple/deep) → Execute search → Broad text-reference search → Cross-repo scope verification → Apply exclusions → Create report → Save results → Update memory

fields: Information Produced: File count, Path to results JSON file, Brief summary
Decisions Made: Search approach used, Search depth mode, Exclusion patterns applied

searchModes.description: Fast search using glob, grep, codebase_search
